sections.h2: What sort of place is Talbot County, Georgia?
sections.html:
A quiet, hilly one. Talbot lies in the west central part of the state, 395 square miles in all and 391 of them dry land, with Talbotton holding the courthouse. Wikipedia records that the legislature carved it out on December 14, 1827 and named it for Matthew Talbot.

The fall line cuts across the county. Ridges of the Pine Mountain range push past 1,000 feet in the far north, while the south is flatter and carries the Fall Line Freeway along State Route 96 between Geneva and Junction City. U.S. 80 and State Route 22 cross it too, and trains run on a CSX subdivision and the Norfolk Southern Columbus District.

Woodland, Geneva and Junction City join Talbotton on the list of municipalities, and part of Manchester reaches in from the neighboring county. Box Springs is a census-designated place, and Po Biddy Crossroads, Tax Crossroads and Centerville are unincorporated names you may see on deeds. Estimated population for July 2025 is 5,709, which works out to about 15 people for each square mile of land.

sections.h2: How do housing figures look for Talbot County?
sections.html:
Occupied homes in Talbot are mostly owned by the people inside them, 79.6% by the Census count, and the middle value for such homes is $117,100 over 2020-2024. Renters face a middle gross rent of $816.

No permits at all in 2025 and a commute of almost 43 minutes paint a county where people live here and drive elsewhere for work, and where nobody is adding houses. With close to three in ten residents past 65, estates are a common reason a house hits the market, and an heir has to deal with the tax office before a buyer ever signs.

sections.h2: Where do Talbot County tax questions get answered?
sections.html:
Start at 38 South Jefferson Avenue in Talbotton, which houses the tax commissioner. Mail goes to P.O. Box 147, and the office website posts weekday hours of 8:00 am to 4:30 pm with a closed hour at noon, plus lines at 706-665-3240 and 706-665-3280.

  • Tax commissioner: billing, collections, mobile home titles, timber tax, tax sales.
  • Tax assessors at 706-665-3377: value, returns, exemptions, appeal paperwork.
  • Commissioners' office, 35 Madison St., 706-665-3220: mobile home location permits.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: intangible tax on recorded loan documents.

You can pay with cash, a check, a money order, or a Visa, MasterCard or Discover card, with a convenience fee on cards. Parcels can be searched through qPublic.

sections.h2: What is the Talbot County billing calendar?
sections.html:
Statements for land, buildings and business personal property typically go out in October with a December 20 due date. The commissioner will take partial payments. Once the date passes, interest runs at prime plus 3%, and a 5% penalty lands every 120 days until it reaches 20%.

Mobile and manufactured homes keep a January-to-April rhythm. Bills are usually mailed early in the year and fall due April 1, a decal goes on the home once the tax is paid, and the return for any home sitting in the county on January 1 is also due April 1. A late return draws a 10% penalty.

The tax office's site also carries a note about trash service: beginning January 1, 2026, the garbage collection fee is $225.00 per year, with extra carts at $137.00 per year. Ask the office whether that charge is attached to your parcel's account so your closing agent catches it.

sections.h2: How is timber taxed in Talbot County?
sections.html:
Standing trees escape tax until they are sold or cut, and then the value used is 100 percent of fair market value times the millage rate. The commissioner's page sorts sales into three kinds.

  • Lump sum sale: the buyer completes form PT-283T and sends the tax and form to the commissioner within five business days, and the buyer is personally liable if the seller does not pay.
  • Unit price sale: a quarterly report is due to the seller and the assessors within 45 days after the quarter ends.
  • Owner harvest: the landowner reports to the assessors within 45 days after the quarter and pays the tax.

A seller with cut or planned timber should ask the office whether a timber account is open before listing.

sections.h2: How does the county sell property for unpaid tax?
sections.html:
The commissioner conducts levy sales under Title 48 and Title 9 of the Georgia code. A property is advertised in the Talbotton New Era four weeks in a row, and the auction follows on the first Tuesday of the month after that run ends.

  • Hours: between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m., at the courthouse on South Washington Avenue.
  • No title guarantee, and the buyer gets no access or rent for at least a year.
  • Winning bids are paid in cash or certified funds right after the sale.
  • Leftover money after taxes and costs becomes excess funds, claimed by written request at 38 South Jefferson Avenue.

A guide to the right of redemption is posted on the commissioner's site. An owner in arrears has time before a sale, and settling the account in a private sale can keep more equity in the seller's hands than an auction would.

sections.h2: Can I dispute a value or claim an exemption in Talbot County?
sections.html:
You can do both through the tax assessors. An owner unhappy with a value files a written dispute with the Board of Assessors and names the route chosen: Board of Equalization, Superior Court, arbitration, or hearing officer. The Department of Revenue's county sheet puts the cutoff at a postmark within 45 days of the notice's mailing.

Returns for real estate are due January 1 through April 1 when something changed, and skipping a required one costs 10% of the value not returned. Business and boat owners file personal property returns, form PT-50P, every year by April 1.

For exemptions, the commissioner's site gives April 1 as the cutoff for the current year, with later filings rolling forward. The state sheet shows no local homestead exemptions in Talbot, so the statewide ones are what an owner claims. Once approved, an exemption keeps renewing until the owner moves or title changes.

sections.h2: What should a Talbot County seller do about tax?
sections.html:
Ask the commissioner for a written payoff on each year still open, and add mobile home and timber accounts if they exist. For an inherited house, find out which years went unpaid before you list, because a recorded lien must be paid at the closing table.

Refund claims are narrow. A request for tax paid by mistake goes in writing to the Board of Commissioners within three years of payment, and the commissioner's page says such refunds depend on errors of fault, not on a disagreement about value. In a sale, the split of the year's bill between buyer and seller is handled on the closing statement.

With so little building and a small buyer pool, a house with a tax cloud is harder to place. A buyer paying cash for the house as it stands can clear the tax balance from your proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Talbot County tax commissioner's office?
faqs.a: At 38 South Jefferson Avenue in Talbotton, with P.O. Box 147 for mail. Doors are open 8:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays, and the office closes from noon to 1:00.

faqs.q: When are Talbot County property tax bills due?
faqs.a: December 20 for real and personal property, with statements typically mailed in October. Mobile homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: Does Talbot County accept partial tax payments?
faqs.a: Yes, according to the commissioner's property tax page. Interest and penalties still build on whatever remains after the due date.

faqs.q: When do Talbot County tax levy sales happen?
faqs.a: On the first Tuesday of a month, after four weeks of advertising in the Talbotton New Era. The courthouse on South Washington Avenue hosts them between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: What is the Talbot County homestead exemption cutoff?
faqs.a: April 1 for the current billing year. The commissioner's FAQ says applications are accepted all year, and one that arrives later applies the following year.
